summary_verdict: The combined bit-exact runtime implementation improves full local encode/decode time. Frozen weight0.4 survives close-rate testing as a useful content-dependent alternative, with actual main-set Q-HQ wins, but not a general high-quality frontier improvement. High-quality holdout coverage remains insufficient. The two exact allocator caches do not materially reduce full encoding cost, so broad promotion/composition was stopped. No optimized HF timing or PBC3.1 release is established.
allocation_verdict: Weight0.4 is a useful content-dependent alternative. Nearest fresh controls within5% yield13/16 main and4/4 holdout MSE wins. Against the best actually measured prior/new control within5%, there are16/19 main and3/4 holdout wins. These direct comparisons retain rate gaps; they are not exact equal-rate claims. Inside released Q-HQ rates, the stronger direct comparison has11/14 main wins but only one holdout match, essentially neutral. Three candidate images remain dominated somewhere on the measured curve.
matched_interpretation: Against the best actual measured control within5% bpp, mean per-image MSE changes-15.62% on19 main cases (16 wins, median-11.94%) and-43.60% on four holdout cases (three wins, median-48.38%). Large holdout improvements against low-budget500k controls, especially15k_kills/old_man_standing, occur outside the released Q-HQ interval. Within that interval, direct main MSE is-10.98% over14 matches (11 wins); holdout is+0.0839% on only pigeons.JPG. Eight main/one holdout cases strictly beat the strongest close control at their actual points, but mario64 is itself dominated by an older lower-rate point; seven main/one holdout such cases remain nondominated in the observed controls. Six of those main cases are in the Q-HQ region. Thus actual-file evidence supports individual frontier extensions, not a universal preset or robust high-quality holdout claim.
allocation_gate: The gate is passed only for a content-dependent alternative with useful observed finite-frontier extensions. It is not passed for a generally better Q-HQ release preset: three measured dominance failures, remaining rate gaps, only one directly matched high-quality holdout case, and material encode cost remain. Ordinary500k35 to allocator remains a rate-for-quality tradeoff (main128.69 to138.46 MSE,0.40329 to0.32107bpp; holdout43.93 to59.02,1.01974 to0.69751). No PBC3.1 all-metric success is claimed.
regression_interpretation: mario64: every one of35 actions changes representation (30 coarser, five lower precision); no early stop. Changed actions retain88.1% of local gain at34.1% raw bits on average, yet final RGB loses detail/efficiency versus250k Balanced, which already has both lower rate and MSE. The fixed-geometry counterpart is worse still, so later evolving geometry partially recovers quality at additional rate; it does not erase the observed dominance. Coarsening and resolution/allocation interaction are supported mechanisms; an isolated percentage of final loss caused by high-frequency detail is not identified. Monet:18/35 representations change (eight coarser, ten lower precision); the allocator runs35 patches versus ordinary33. Changed actions retain84.0% local gain/51.1% raw bits. This is not premature stopping. Unlike the other named cases, new close ordinary controls favor the allocator(-8.64% measured MSE against the best5%-near point); the prior interpolated envelope still predicts+12.02% loss. It remains an interpolation/control-family issue rather than a newly verified direct loss, and must not be called fixed or assigned one precision-only cause. Eiffel: nine of20 emitted actions change (seven lower precision, two coarser), retaining93.65% local gain/70.65% raw bits. The modified trajectory stops at20 versus ordinary23; both final MSE and bpp worsen (25.22/1.82813 to27.44/1.88780). A fresh p25 control at1.81396bpp/25.04869MSE dominates it; this is a verified representation/trajectory/stop failure, not merely a sparse interpolation artifact. Pigeon: all35 actions change (20 coarser,15 lower precision), without early stopping, retaining90.95% local gain/51.76% raw bits. It beats a nearby low-budget500k control but is dominated by released Balanced at0.009133bpp/51.3971MSE versus0.012250/53.6133. Its main failure is extra500k representation cost relative to an effective low-rate250k trajectory, with coarsening/precision and subsequent geometry interacting. No unique model-capacity or entropy-statistic cause is proved for any case.
efficiency_verdict: No substantial allocator cost reduction was established. On the six-image uninstrumented screen, ordinary/frozen/composite encode means of case medians are0.76551/0.82826/0.82083s. Frozen allocation costs8.20% more than ordinary; the exact composite saves only0.90% of allocator time (five/six median wins), below the predetermined2% promotion gate and comparable to repeat variation. Projection alone is+1.04%, before-SSE alone-0.41%. No full-dataset cache timing or optional fast-runtime allocation combination was run.
efficiency_interpretation: The composite saves about7.44ms from the frozen allocator's828.26ms mean; its net overhead above ordinary remains55.31ms (7.23%), versus62.75ms (8.20%) originally on this six-image set. It nominally removes about11.85% of the incremental difference but only0.90% of the complete encoder wall, so this is not a substantial full-codec result. Average within-case encode CV is1.58% frozen and2.26% composite (projection3.75%, before-SSE4.92%). Projection avoids35 repeated projections and before-SSE70 repeated reductions on cat, but function savings are too small relative to the remaining search/model/resampling/quantization work and bookkeeping. All tested caches preserve exact files, patch order, policy counts, raw-bit totals and gain totals. The first unequal-path profile/timing runs were corrected and excluded, not used to support these values.
fast_interpretation: Combined fast-runtime allocator cost was not measured: the cache composite failed its predeclared substantial-saving gate, so the optional broad composition was stopped. The independently confirmed fast runtime remains valid, but its percentages are not added to allocation timings or used to infer an unmeasured release/HF cost. A already measures the combined runtime without allocation; C's only allocator cost result is the same-underlying-runtime six-image screen.
efficiency_gate: Stop this cost branch. The methods are exact operation-reuse demonstrations, but not ready for production on their measured benefit/complexity. No third optimization, broad cache confirmation, new selector, proxy or weight was tried. Retaining files exactly retains RD wins and failures; it does not repair the allocation gate or establish an overall faster release.
efficiency_scope: The composite missed the2% screen promotion gate, so no full25-image cache timing or optional fast-runtime allocator composition was run. The negative result and predeclared gate are retained.
incremental_cost_answer: The same-runtime uninstrumented six-image screen measures ordinary0.76551s versus frozen allocator0.82826s: incremental62.75ms/+8.20%. Corrected cProfile shows extra representations plus more actual search/model steps; local candidate work alone cannot explain the whole difference. The full25-image nearest-rate confirmation separately measures main0.64256s ordinary versus0.93821s allocator, and holdout0.45380s versus0.70176s; those controls often request fewer patches and therefore measure rate-matched operating-point compute, not equal35-budget allocator-only overhead.
exact_cost_answer: Decisions/files are preserved, but cost is not substantially reduced. Projection+before-SSE gives0.82083s versus frozen0.82826s(-0.90%) on six main images/three repeats; projection alone+1.04%, before-SSE-0.41%. This failed the frozen2% gate, so no broad timing or fast allocator composition was promoted.
pass5_answer: Prioritize independent images with actual tightly matched ordinary controls specifically in the Quality-to-HQ region, keeping the allocator frozen and retaining the named dominance failures; this is the remaining RD validation gap. Separately, obtain explicit authorization for the minimal bounded benchmark extension on the existing HF Space and validate grid/search/metric-free runtime modes in one worker before any production change. Only pursue one targeted representation/geometry hypothesis if these direct high-quality results justify it; a classifier or more fixed weights is not yet supported. A PBC4 rewrite or broad native decoder effort is lower priority than these measured gaps.
stop_answer: The two screened allocator cache mechanisms should stop at their negative substantial-saving gate; do not spend a full25-image timing suite trying to turn a0.9% point estimate into a release claim.
classification: Verified local output-preserving runtime improvement: combined grid/MSE-opt-out/search reuse. RD tradeoff versus equal-budget ordinary encoder and useful content-dependent finite-frontier alternative: frozen allocator0.4. Confirmed measured dominance failures: mario64,eiffel,pigeon; Monet's direct and interpolated comparisons disagree and remain explicitly separate. High-quality holdout generalization and optimized HF CPU benefit: inconclusive/unvalidated. Allocator cache cost reduction: exact but too small for promotion, with projection's point estimate regressing. No strict all-metric PBC3.1 improvement or production acceptance.
